verdict.headline: BUY / ADD — CONTRACTED CASH FLOW COMPOUNDING BEHIND A VOLATILE GAAP HEADLINE
verdict.subhead: QUALITY 0.5  |  GROWTH 1.0  |  PEER 1.0      |      TECHNICALS CONSTRUCTIVE — UPTREND INTACT, TARGET ABOVE PRICE
verdict.summary: LNG scores 2.5/3.0 — a downgrade from the 3.0 carried on the triage card, and the reason is worth stating plainly. The business is producing records: Q2 exports of 672 TBtu across 184 cargoes, up 20% year on year, and management raised full-year guidance for the second consecutive quarter — consolidated adjusted EBITDA to $7.9–8.4B (midpoint +$650M) and distributable cash flow to $5.3–5.8B (midpoint +$550M), with the new low end above the old high end. What a screener cannot see is that GAAP is unusable here: a −$3.50B loss in Q1 2026 and a +$3.07B profit in Q2 on steadily rising revenue leave six-month net income at −$434M, while six-month adjusted EBITDA rose 26% to $4.14B. Quality scores 0.5 rather than 1.0 because no reported margin series is expanding — gross margin has gone 83.87% (FY23) to 36.85% (ttm) — and free cash flow has fallen to $2.79B from $6.30B in FY23. The FCF decline is deliberate growth capex on Corpus Christi Stage 3 and is defensible, but the rubric asks whether margins are clearly expanding off a healthy base, and on the reported numbers they are not. Growth and peer position both earn a full 1.0. At 2.5 with a constructive overlay and a consensus target 6.2% above the entry, the plan is unchanged: LONG STOCK, no calls.

assessment.heading: ASSESSMENT: THE DIVERGENCE IS INSIDE THE INCOME STATEMENT, NOT BETWEEN PRICE AND FUNDAMENTALS
assessment.text: The usual actionable setups are strong fundamentals against a weak tape, or a strong tape against deteriorating fundamentals. Cheniere is neither. Price and operations are pointing the same way — the tape is in an uptrend and adjusted EBITDA, distributable cash flow and export volumes are all rising. The divergence is between two lines of the same income statement: GAAP net income, which swung $6.57B between Q1 and Q2 2026 on the fair value of IFM derivative positions, and consolidated adjusted EBITDA, which rose 26% over the same six months. Anyone screening on reported earnings, trailing P/E or GAAP margin gets a false reading of this company in both directions — spectacular in Q2, catastrophic in Q1. That is a reason to score Quality honestly at 0.5 while still buying the operating business, not a reason to treat the GAAP figures as the signal.

catalyst.title: The US LNG Export Buildout — Is Cheniere Still the Right Horse?

left.title: THE OPPORTUNITY (today's leader, and it is producing)

blocks.heading: 1. Stage 3 is converting capex into volume, on schedule
bullets: Substantial completion of the sixth train was achieved in June 2026, and first LNG production from the seventh train was described as expected imminently. Q2 exports reached 672 TBtu across 184 cargoes, up 20% year on year, with management crediting Stage 3 acceleration and improved reliability.

blocks.heading: 2. Guidance raised twice in a single year
bullets: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance went from $7.25–7.75B to $7.9–8.4B, and distributable cash flow from $4.75–5.25B to $5.3–5.8B. The new low end sits above the previous high end on both measures — the strongest single signal in the rubric.

blocks.heading: 3. Capacity leadership is real, and operating
bullets: Roughly 56 mtpa across Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi with about 5 mtpa more under construction. Unlike most of the peer set, this capacity is exporting cargoes today rather than awaiting a 2027–28 start date.

blocks.heading: 4. Cash is being returned, not merely earned
bullets: $3.19B of buybacks over the trailing twelve months against a $60.31B market cap, plus $461M of dividends. The payout ratio is 16.32% and the dividend rose 11% to $2.22 — the return is funded, not stretched.

blocks.heading: 1. Venture Global is built to overtake it
bullets: VG reports over 100 mtpa in production, construction or development against Cheniere's ~56 mtpa, and industry coverage projects it to pass Cheniere as the largest US exporter by 2030. Cheniere leads today; it is not obviously the structural winner of the next decade.

blocks.heading: 2. The GAAP headline will keep swinging
bullets: −$3.50B in Q1, +$3.07B in Q2. Any screen, index rule or valuation model keyed to reported earnings or trailing P/E will misprice this company periodically in both directions, which can move the stock for reasons unrelated to the business.

blocks.heading: 3. Free cash flow has halved while the trains are built
bullets: $2.79B ttm against $6.30B in FY23, on $3.35B of trailing capex. FCF margin is 13.34% versus 20.42% in FY24. This is a defensible growth investment, but it is not yet a cash-return story, and it leans on a levered balance sheet — $27.97B of debt, D/E 2.43, current ratio 0.87.

blocks.heading: 4. Consensus is already close to the price
bullets: The $308.90 average target is only 6.2% above the entry, and the low target of $255 sits 12.3% below it. The Street high of $340 is the stretch case, not the base case — this is a position to size, not to press.

verdict.text: LNG VERDICT: STILL THE RIGHT HORSE FOR 2026 — NOT AUTOMATICALLY FOR 2030. Cheniere is the largest operating US LNG exporter, it is the one converting construction into cargoes right now, and it raised guidance twice this year while buying back $3.19B of stock. That is what the screener caught. The honest caveats are that Venture Global's development pipeline is roughly twice Cheniere's operating capacity and is projected to overtake it by 2030, that reported margins and free cash flow are both falling on the numbers as published, and that consensus sits only 6.2% above the entry.

finalVerdict.reasoning: The score fell from 3.0 on the triage card to 2.5 on full verification, entirely in Part 1. That is the finding of this report, not a rounding difference: Cheniere's reported gross margin has compressed from 83.87% in FY23 to 36.85% trailing, and free cash flow has fallen from $6.30B to $2.79B. Both are explicable — the margin swing is mark-to-market on IFM derivative positions, and the cash flow decline is $3.35B of growth capex on Corpus Christi Stage 3 — but the rubric asks whether margins are clearly expanding off a healthy base, and no reported series says they are. At 2.5 with a constructive overlay the plan does not change: this remains a LONG STOCK position at the same entry, stop and target. What changes is the honesty of the file. If Stage 3 completes and free cash flow recovers toward the FY23 level while adjusted EBITDA holds the raised guidance, Part 1 returns to 1.0 on the next re-verification. If Venture Global's pipeline starts converting while Cheniere sanctions nothing new, Part 3 is the score that falls next.
